facts.fact: Madagascar-Tribune, a Madagascar news site, published a piece questioning the government's cybercrime bill n°042/2026, saying the permanent access powers of its new digital police (article 75) raise issues of public freedoms and of balance with freedom of expression, and contrasting it with the stalled access-to-information bill; the document is dated 2026-09-03 and gives no earlier date.

facts.fact: CPJ reports that journalist Fernand Cello was arrested on 29 January 2025, then charged on 30 January with spreading false news and undermining national security and put in pretrial detention over a Facebook post about President Rajoelina.

Amnesty International says at least nine Gen Z leaders were arbitrarily arrested in April 2026 simply for being in a WhatsApp group or messaging an opposition figure or whistleblower, and some were accused of plotting to assassinate the president.
The Presidency said on 8 January 2026 that judicial proceedings were under way against people, accounts or pages accused of insulting and inciting hatred against senior state officials online.
Transparency International Initiative Madagascar published a critical report on bill 042/2026, pointing to grey areas in the data-access powers of the proposed UPIN unit, as reported by Tech-Connect.
